articles.title: Stablecoins have stopped growing. So why is usage still rising?
articles.description: Standard Chartered now expects the stablecoin market to reach $2 trillion by 2030, two years later than it first projected. The bank made the change after total stablecoin supply stalled at roughly $309 billion this year, according to Cointelegraph, which was shown the report. Read quickly, a “$2 trillion” headline sounds bullish. It is really a delay. The more interesting part of the report is the bank’s argument that stablecoins are still being used more, even though the market has stopped getting bigger. Understanding how both can be true is one of the most useful ideas in crypto right now. Market size and usage are two different things A stablecoin is a crypto token designed to hold a steady value, usually one US dollar, backed by reserves held by the issuer. Because each token is meant to be worth $1, a stablecoin’s market capitalisation is in practice the number of tokens in circulation. That figure tells you how many stablecoin dollars exist. It does not tell you how hard those dollars are working. Think of a taxi fleet. The number of cars on the road can stay flat while the number of trips rises, because each car is busier. Geoffrey Kendrick, Standard Chartered’s head of digital assets research, describes stablecoins in the same terms: supply growth has slowed, but existing tokens are changing hands more often as their uses widen. Economists call this velocity. The practical point for readers is that a flat market cap chart, on its own, does not show demand fading. It can mean the same pool of money is circulating faster. Four markets, not one Kendrick splits stablecoins into four separate markets, each with its own leader: Emerging-market savings: Tether’s USDT dominates, used by people holding dollars outside their local banking system. Developed-market payments: Circle’s USDC leads. Crypto trading: USDC and Ethena’s USDe hold strong positions. Payments between AI agents: a much smaller market, also led by USDC. This matters because “the stablecoin market” is often treated as one race between USDT and USDC. On the bank’s framing, the two largest tokens are mostly doing different jobs for different users. Why reserve yield could decide the winners Issuers typically hold their reserves in cash and short-term government debt, which earns interest. Kendrick argues that how issuers and payment networks share that income could determine who gains market share. He expects the fiercest competition in developed-market payments, where challengers such as USDG, M^0 and stablecoin networks run by groups of banks are building alternatives to existing payment rails. A network that passes more of the yield on to the businesses using it has a clear selling point. The regulatory calendar The US rulebook is still being written. Since the GENIUS Act passed in 2025, regulators have proposed rules covering issuance, reserves and consumer protection. Three proposals stand out: Treasury licensing: an August proposal would restrict US stablecoin issuance to federally or state-authorised issuers, with licensing expected to take effect in January 2027. Deposit insurance: a Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) proposal would exclude stablecoin holders from pass-through deposit insurance, meaning their holdings would not be treated like insured bank deposits. Accounting: the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB), which sets US accounting standards, proposed an update in August that could change how companies report some stablecoins on their balance sheets. Payments firm Tempo said this could make it easier for businesses to use stablecoins for settlement. The accounting change is easy to overlook. Corporate adoption of a payment tool often depends less on the technology than on whether the finance team can book it cleanly. What could change the interpretation The velocity argument relies on usage data continuing to grow. If transaction activity flattened alongside supply, the “same dollars, working harder” reading would weaken, and the delayed forecast could start to look optimistic. On the other side, a fresh rise in supply would suggest new money is arriving. Clearer US licensing rules from 2027 could help that by giving larger institutions the certainty they need to issue or hold stablecoins at scale. What to watch next Watch two numbers together rather than one: total stablecoin supply and transaction volume. Rising volume on flat supply supports Standard Chartered’s view. Falling volume on flat supply would be a warning sign. Then watch the rule-making. The final shape of the Treasury licensing rules ahead of January 2027, and whether FASB finalises its accounting proposal, will show how quickly regulated institutions can move into the payments market. The practical takeaway is that a stalled market cap does not by itself mean the stablecoin story has stalled. Look at how money moves, not just how much of it exists. This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

articles.title: SMS Tan Kiat How, Rosianna Silalahi and Glenda Gloria to speak at PRISM Summit 2026
articles.description: Senior Minister of State Tan Kiat How to attend as Guest-of-Honour at the 12 November summit, which will bring together leaders from across public relations, journalism, business and technology SINGAPORE - Media OutReach Newswire - 15 October 2026 - The Institute of Public Relations of Singapore (IPRS) has announced the keynote speakers for the Media OutReach Newswire PRISM Summit 2026, taking place on 12 November at METT Singapore. Mr Tan Kiat How, Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and National Development, will attend as Guest-of-Honour. Held under the theme "From Message to Mandate", the Summit will examine how communications professionals can move beyond message delivery to influence organisational decisions, safeguard reputation and build stakeholder trust in an environment increasingly shaped by artificial intelligence, fragmented media and heightened scrutiny. The programme brings together perspectives from newsrooms, corporate leadership, technology and the communications industry to address a central question: how can communications leaders maintain credibility and demonstrate their strategic value when the information landscape is changing faster than ever? Notable keynote speakers include Rosianna Silalahi, President Director of KompasTV, whose session, "Holding the Line: What Newsrooms Need from Communicators", will draw on the Indonesian broadcaster's experience navigating demonstrations, external pressure and the growing challenges of verifying information. Her contribution will examine the responsibilities journalists and communicators share in protecting information integrity, maintaining editorial independence, and establishing accountability for AI-generated content. The relationship between media credibility and organisational reputation will also feature in the keynote by Glenda Gloria, Co-Founder and Executive Editor of Rappler, who will deliver "Keepers of the Record", reflecting on journalism's role in an era of disinformation and declining trust, and what the changing media landscape means for communications professionals. Beyond the newsroom, the Summit will consider how communications can deliver greater strategic value to organisations. Terence Lyons, Founder and CEO of TSC.ai, will examine how stakeholder intelligence can help organisations anticipate emerging issues and understand influence, while Wendy Wang, Founder of getUGC.io, will explore the evolving relationship between creators, communities and brand trust. Another focus will be the growing influence of artificial intelligence on how organisations are discovered and understood. Shaad Hamid, General Manager, Singapore at GrowthOps Asia, will examine the relationship between earned media and AI visibility, while Emma Dale, Co-Founder and Managing Director of Prospect Resourcing, will consider the human judgement, trust and leadership that remain essential as AI becomes more embedded in communications work. Jennifer Kok, Founder and CEO of Media OutReach Newswire, will deliver the Title Sponsor Keynote, "The Golden Age of PR: Why an AI-Enabled Global Newswire Matters More Than Ever", exploring the role of earned media and newswire distribution in building brand trust and visibility in an AI-driven environment. The programme will culminate in the unveiling of findings from the inaugural Singapore State of PR and Communications Survey, jointly conducted by Media OutReach Newswire and IPRS. The research will offer insights into how communications practitioners view changing PR dynamics, the evolving media landscape, AI visibility, and their use of AI tools in daily workflows. Other speakers include Liu Xiaowei, Co-Founder of Retension; Nicholas Leong, Head of Media Relations, Asia Pacific at DHL; Raju Chellam, Editor-in-Chief of the AI Ethics & Governance Body of Knowledge; Emily Poon, CEO of the Singapore Institute of Directors; Shefali Srinivas, Head of Business Communications, APAC at Meta; Esther An, Chief Sustainability Officer at City Developments Limited; and Brian Fletcher, Director, Public Policy APJ at CrowdStrike. PRISM Summit 2026 is supported by Title Sponsor Media OutReach Newswire, Coffee & Silver Sponsor Notified, Silver Sponsors Isentia and Truescope, Official PR Agency Pinpoint and Venue Partner METT Singapore. Supporting Partners include Edge Digital, the Public Relations and Communications Association (PRCA), World Communication Forum Association (WCFA), Davos Communications Summit & Awards, Asia Pacific PR Network (APRN), Singapore Institute of Directors (SID) and Singapore Press Club (SPC). Media Partners include Humas Indonesia and PR Indonesia. Full speaker line-up The PRISM Summit 2026 speaker line-up comprises: Anita Kapoor - HostRoss Gan - President, IPRS; Chief Communications Officer, Bitdeer TechnologiesJennifer Kok - Founder & CEO, Media OutReach NewswireRaju Chellam - Editor-in-Chief, AI Ethics & Governance Body of KnowledgeIllka Gobius - Founder & Managing Director, Pinpoint PRKathy O'Brien - Managing Director, Red Shoe CommunicationsLee Nugent - Head of Communications, Asia-Pacific & Japan, EverpureEmily Poon - CEO, Singapore Institute of DirectorsLiu Xiaowei - Co-Founder, RetensionTerence Lyons - Founder & CEO, TSC.aiBrian Fletcher - Director, Public Policy APJ, CrowdStrikeNaeema Ismail - Founder, The Reset PracticeShefali Srinivas - Head of Business Communications, APAC, MetaGlenda Gloria - Co-Founder & Executive Editor, RapplerRosianna Silalahi - Editor-in-Chief, KompasTVGlenn van Zutphen - Founder & CEO, VanMedia GroupWendy Wang - Founder, getUGC.ioPrashant Saxena - VP of Revenue & Insights, Southeast Asia, iSentiaCollin Tio - Associate Director, KOBEAngel Turner - Senior Manager, Brand Marketing, World Scout BureauShaad Hamid - General Manager, Singapore, GrowthOps AsiaCheryl Heng - Associate Editor, Citywire AsiaVoal Voal Wong - Managing Partner, IN.FOMMelissa Ang - Strategic Account Director, NotifiedPamela Phua - Managing Partner, Southeast Asia, Media OutReach NewswireKelvin Koh - Managing Director, Truescope SingaporeNicholas Leong - Head of Media Relations, Asia Pacific, DHLEmma Dale - Co-Founder & Managing Director, Prospect ResourcingEsther An - Chief Sustainability Officer, City Developments LimitedCindy Lim - PRISM Summit 2026 Chair; Head of Audience & Communications, Singapore Symphony Group Registration is open, with special rates available to IPRS members and partners. For more information and registration, visit the Summit website. articles.description: Senior Minister of State Tan Kiat How to attend as Guest-of-Honour at the 12 November summit, which will bring together leaders from across public relations, journalism, business and technology SINGAPORE – Media OutReach Newswire – 15 October 2026 — The Institute of Public Relations of Singapore (IPRS) has announced the keynote speakers for the Media OutReach Newswire PRISM Summit 2026, taking place on 12 November at METT Singapore. Mr Tan Kiat How, Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and National Development, will attend as Guest-of-Honour. Held under the theme "From Message to Mandate", the Summit will examine how communications professionals can move beyond message delivery to influence organisational decisions, safeguard reputation and build stakeholder trust in an environment increasingly shaped by artificial intelligence, fragmented media and heightened scrutiny. The programme brings together perspectives from newsrooms, corporate leadership, technology and the communications industry to address a central question: how can communications leaders maintain credibility and demonstrate their strategic value when the information landscape is changing faster than ever? Notable keynote speakers include Rosianna Silalahi, President Director of KompasTV, whose session, "Holding the Line: What Newsrooms Need from Communicators", will draw on the Indonesian broadcaster's experience navigating demonstrations, external pressure and the growing challenges of verifying information. Her contribution will examine the responsibilities journalists and communicators share in protecting information integrity, maintaining editorial independence, and establishing accountability for AI-generated content. The relationship between media credibility and organisational reputation will also feature in the keynote by Glenda Gloria, Co-Founder and Executive Editor of Rappler, who will deliver "Keepers of the Record", reflecting on journalism's role in an era of disinformation and declining trust, and what the changing media landscape means for communications professionals. Beyond the newsroom, the Summit will consider how communications can deliver greater strategic value to organisations. Terence Lyons, Founder and CEO of TSC.ai, will examine how stakeholder intelligence can help organisations anticipate emerging issues and understand influence, while Wendy Wang, Founder of getUGC.io, will explore the evolving relationship between creators, communities and brand trust. Another focus will be the growing influence of artificial intelligence on how organisations are discovered and understood. Shaad Hamid, General Manager, Singapore at GrowthOps Asia, will examine the relationship between earned media and AI visibility, while Emma Dale, Co-Founder and Managing Director of Prospect Resourcing, will consider the human judgement, trust and leadership that remain essential as AI becomes more embedded in communications work. Jennifer Kok, Founder and CEO of Media OutReach Newswire, will deliver the Title Sponsor Keynote, "The Golden Age of PR: Why an AI-Enabled Global Newswire Matters More Than Ever", exploring the role of earned media and newswire distribution in building brand trust and visibility in an AI-driven environment. The programme will culminate in the unveiling of findings from the inaugural Singapore State of PR and Communications Survey, jointly conducted by Media OutReach Newswire and IPRS. The research will offer insights into how communications practitioners view changing PR dynamics, the evolving media landscape, AI visibility, and their use of AI tools in daily workflows. Other speakers include Liu Xiaowei, Co-Founder of Retension; Nicholas Leong, Head of Media Relations, Asia Pacific at DHL; Raju Chellam, Editor-in-Chief of the AI Ethics & Governance Body of Knowledge; Emily Poon, CEO of the Singapore Institute of Directors; Shefali Srinivas, Head of Business Communications, APAC at Meta; Esther An, Chief Sustainability Officer at City Developments Limited; and Brian Fletcher, Director, Public Policy APJ at CrowdStrike. PRISM Summit 2026 is supported by Title Sponsor Media OutReach Newswire, Coffee & Silver Sponsor Notified, Silver Sponsors Isentia and Truescope, Official PR Agency Pinpoint and Venue Partner METT Singapore. Supporting Partners include Edge Digital, the Public Relations and Communications Association (PRCA), World Communication Forum Association (WCFA), Davos Communications Summit & Awards, Asia Pacific PR Network (APRN), Singapore Institute of Directors (SID) and Singapore Press Club (SPC). Media Partners include Humas Indonesia and PR Indonesia. Full speaker line-up The PRISM Summit 2026 speaker line-up comprises: Anita Kapoor – Host Ross Gan — President, IPRS; Chief Communications Officer, Bitdeer Technologies Jennifer Kok — Founder & CEO, Media OutReach Newswire Raju Chellam — Editor-in-Chief, AI Ethics & Governance Body of Knowledge Illka Gobius — Founder & Managing Director, Pinpoint PR Kathy O'Brien — Managing Director, Red Shoe Communications Lee Nugent — Head of Communications, Asia-Pacific & Japan, Everpure Emily Poon — CEO, Singapore Institute of Directors Liu Xiaowei — Co-Founder, Retension Terence Lyons — Founder & CEO, TSC.ai Brian Fletcher — Director, Public Policy APJ, CrowdStrike Naeema Ismail — Founder, The Reset Practice Shefali Srinivas — Head of Business Communications, APAC, Meta Glenda Gloria — Co-Founder & Executive Editor, Rappler Rosianna Silalahi — Editor-in-Chief, KompasTV Glenn van Zutphen — Founder & CEO, VanMedia Group Wendy Wang — Founder, getUGC.io Prashant Saxena — VP of Revenue & Insights, Southeast Asia, iSentia Collin Tio — Associate Director, KOBE Angel Turner — Senior Manager, Brand Marketing, World Scout Bureau Shaad Hamid — General Manager, Singapore, GrowthOps Asia Cheryl Heng — Associate Editor, Citywire Asia Voal Voal Wong — Managing Partner, IN.FOM Melissa Ang — Strategic Account Director, Notified Pamela Phua — Managing Partner, Southeast Asia, Media OutReach Newswire Kelvin Koh — Managing Director, Truescope Singapore Nicholas Leong — Head of Media Relations, Asia Pacific, DHL Emma Dale — Co-Founder & Managing Director, Prospect Resourcing Esther An — Chief Sustainability Officer, City Developments Limited Cindy Lim — PRISM Summit 2026 Chair; Head of Audience & Communications, Singapore Symphony Group Registration is open, with special rates available to IPRS members and partners. For more information and registration, visit the Summit website. articles.title: Which Apple Home Devices Get Siri AI, and When
articles.description: There's been some confusion about which of Apple's new and existing home devices will support Siri AI and when, because Siri AI isn't going to be available at launch on some products. Devices With Siri AI HomeView - Available at launch (November 13) Apple TV 4K (4th generation) - Available at launch (November 13) Apple TV 4K (3rd generation) - Available in tvOS 27.2 Apple TV 4K (2nd generation) - Available in tvOS 27.2 HomePod mini 2 - Ships October 30, Siri AI coming in a future software update Despite a report from CNET suggesting the first HomePod mini would support Siri AI, Apple has since confirmed that's not the case. No Siri AI Support Original HomePod mini Original HomePod Original Apple TV 4K (no tvOS 27) Apple TV HD (no tvOS 27) Unconfirmed HomePod 2 - Possibly coming, with mentions in website metadata Siri AI Requirements On the HomePod and Apple TV 4K models that support Siri AI, the home owner in the Home app must have an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad on the latest version of the software. Siri AI has to be turned on, and it has to be set to a supported language. Other members of the household don't need an Apple Intelligence-enabled device once Siri AI is turned on, except for personal requests. HomeView does not require an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad for Siri AI, except for requests that use personal context. Siri AI for HomeView, Apple TV 4K, and HomePod mini 2 is English only and is limited to the United States, Australia, Canada, India, New Zealand, Singapore, South Africa, and the UK at launch. EU Restrictions Siri AI is not available in the EU on the iPhone and iPad‌, so Siri AI won't be available for home devices that support it. HomeView isn't even launching in the EU. Siri AI Beta Apple is still calling Siri AI a beta, and it will be in beta when it's available on HomeView, Apple TV 4K, and HomePod mini 2‌.
